subject: POC trial success criteria & KPIs — next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & proposed POC success criteria (next steps)

Hey Liam — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the kickoff.

High-level POC objective:
- Validate that Redwood can meet Atlas Payments' real-time payment QA assistant needs at production scale while keeping unit cost predictable.

Proposed success criteria / KPIs (please confirm or adjust):
- Latency: p95 < 200ms (in-region) for 256-token edits/generations
- Throughput: sustain 100 RPS for peak load windows with autoscale handling spikes to 250 RPS
- Cost: average cost per 1000 tokens <= $0.50 (i.e., ~$0.0005 / token) when using recommended batching/quantization profiles
- Quality: >= 92% accuracy on labeled evaluation set (we'll provide 1k labeled examples) and <3% regression vs your baseline on critical intents
- Reliability: <1% error rate, fallback behavior defined for model timeouts

What we need from Atlas to start the trial:
1) A de-identified sample dataset (1k items) and priority intents
2) Security/compliance contact for questionnaire and firewall/VPC details
3) Confirmation of internal owner(s) and procurement timeline

Proposed timeline:
- Kickoff: week of 2029-05-22
- Trial: 2 weeks (config + run) with mid-point checkpoint
- Wrap & evaluation: week following trial to review KPIs and next steps

I've attached a short POC evaluation plan (POC-Eval-Plan-Atlas-v1.pdf) with measurement details and an example runbook. Can you confirm the proposed KPIs and the internal owner so we can lock dates?

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlas-payments.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@atlas-payments.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & proposed POC success criteria (next steps)

Thanks Jordan — solid recap. A few quick adjustments from our side and answers to your asks: 

- Latency: if possible we'd like to target p95 < 150ms for our high-priority flows (payment verification path). If that's realistic with your suggested batching/quantization configs, great — otherwise keep 200ms as a fallback.
- Throughput: 100 RPS sustained sounds right for initial testing; we need the ability to spike to 400 RPS for short bursts during peak hours.
- Cost: the rough cost target works; we'll validate against our internal model.
- Quality: we'll share the 1k labeled examples by Monday; our internal baseline accuracy is ~90% on the same intents.

Owners: Sara Patel will be our technical owner for the trial (she's cc'd). Procurement: procurement expects to approve a short-term SOW by the end of next week — pending standard security questionnaire items.

Questions for Redwood:
- Can you confirm what sample size (RPS * duration) you'd use to validate throughput/latency?
- Can you provide a short runbook for the initial setup (networking, auth, sample workload)?

I'll confirm internal availability for kickoff next week once procurement gives the green light.

— Liam
Liam O'Connor
Director, Engineering — Integrations
Atlas Payments
liam@atlas-payments.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlas-payments.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 May 2029 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & proposed POC success criteria (next steps)

Thanks Liam — helpful notes. Attached is a short runbook and an updated POC run checklist (POC-Runbook-Redwood.docx). Answering your questions inline: 

- Throughput validation plan: we typically run a 1-hour soak at target sustained RPS (100 RPS) and then run spike tests where we ramp to the burst target (400 RPS) in 5-minute windows. We'll collect p50/p95/p99 and error rates.
- Sample size for stable latency readings: 30k requests across different payload sizes (we'll provide a generator script).
- Runbook includes networking/auth steps (API keys, VPC peering instructions) and a sample workload script.

Proposed owners and responsibilities:
- Jordan Blake: infra setup, test harness, and day-to-day trial coordination
- Marissa Cole: evaluation metrics, dashboarding, and quality checks (will coordinate labeled evals)
- Neha Kapoor: security questionnaire owner and compliance liaison

Proposed timeline (firming up):
- Kickoff call + network setup: 2029-05-22
- Data ingest & baseline test: 2029-05-23 to 2029-05-24
- Trial run / soak + spike tests: 2029-05-27 to 2029-05-31
- Mid-trial checkpoint: 2029-05-29
- Final evaluation & wrap: 2029-06-03

Attachments: POC-Runbook-Redwood.docx, sample-dataset-1k.csv

Jordan — can you provision a short-lived test environment and share access details by Monday? We'll block the mid-trial checkpoint on both calendars.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
